Objective To determine the feasibility and biologic correlations of dynamic susceptibility contrast (DSC), dynamic contrast enhanced (DCE), and quantitative maps derived from contrast leakage effects obtained simultaneously in gliomas using dynamic spin-and-gradient-echo echoplanar imaging (dynamic SAGE-EPI) during a single contrast injection. Materials and methods Thirty-eight patients with enhancing brain gliomas were prospectively imaged with dynamic SAGE-EPI, which was processed to compute traditional DSC metrics (normalized relative cerebral blood flow [nrCBV], percentage of signal recovery [PSR]), DCE metrics (volume transfer constant [ K trans ], extravascular compartment [ v e ]), and leakage effect metrics: Δ R 2,ss * (reflecting T 2 *-leakage effects), Δ R 1,ss (reflecting T 1 -leakage effects), and the transverse relaxivity at tracer equilibrium ( TRATE , reflecting the balance between Δ R 2,ss * and Δ R 1,ss ). These metrics were compared between patient subgroups (treatment-naïve [TN] vs recurrent [R]) and biological features (IDH status, Ki67 expression). Results In IDH wild-type gliomas (IDH wt —i.e., glioblastomas), previous exposure to treatment determined lower TRATE ( p = 0.002), as well as higher PSR ( p = 0.006), K trans ( p = 0.17), Δ R 1,ss ( p = 0.035), v e ( p = 0.006), and ADC ( p = 0.016). In IDH-mutant gliomas (IDH m ), previous treatment determined higher K trans and Δ R 1,ss ( p = 0.026). In TN-gliomas, dynamic SAGE-EPI metrics tended to be influenced by IDH status ( p ranging 0.09–0.14). TRATE values above 142 mM −1 s −1 were exclusively seen in TN-IDH wt , and, in TN-gliomas, this cutoff had 89% sensitivity and 80% specificity as a predictor of Ki67 > 10%. Conclusions Dynamic SAGE-EPI enables simultaneous quantification of brain tumor perfusion and permeability, as well as mapping of novel metrics related to cytoarchitecture ( TRATE ) and blood–brain barrier disruption (Δ R 1,ss ), with a single contrast injection. Clinical relevance statement Simultaneous DSC and DCE analysis with dynamic SAGE-EPI reduces scanning time and contrast dose, respectively alleviating concerns about imaging protocol length and gadolinium adverse effects and accumulation, while providing novel leakage effect metrics reflecting blood–brain barrier disruption and tumor tissue cytoarchitecture. Key Points • Traditionally, perfusion and permeability imaging for brain tumors requires two separate contrast injections and acquisitions. • Dynamic spin-and-gradient-echo echoplanar imaging enables simultaneous perfusion and permeability imaging. • Dynamic spin-and-gradient-echo echoplanar imaging provides new image contrasts reflecting blood–brain barrier disruption and cytoarchitecture characteristics. Ellingson Benjamin M. issue-copyright-statement © European Society of Radiology 2024 Introduction Brain gliomas are characterized by heterogeneous prognosis, depending on biological and molecular features [ 1 , 2 ] and on a variable response to treatment [ 3 – 5 ]. Aggressive tumors rely on a more intense neoangiogenesis, resulting in a dysfunctional neovasculature with blood–brain barrier (BBB) breakdown [ 6 – 9 ]. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) can non-invasively quantify vascularization and BBB permeability in vivo, using two separate techniques based on contrast agent (CA) administration: dynamic susceptibility contrast (DSC), a T 2 *-weighted gradient-echo (GE) sequence, and dynamic contrast enhanced (DCE), a T 1 -weighted sequence [ 10 ]. While DSC perfusion imaging yields rCBV (relative cerebral blood volume), reflecting vascular density [ 11 ], DCE permeability imaging allows to compute K trans (volume transfer constant), representing the rate of CA leakage and therefore BBB permeability [ 12 ]. These techniques can aid glioma grading [ 13 – 15 ], molecular profiling [ 16 – 19 ], differential diagnosis [ 10 , 20 – 24 ], and the distinction between treatment effects and tumor recurrence [ 10 , 24 – 27 ], and have become part of the clinical brain tumor work-up in many neuroimaging centers [ 28 ]. However, performing perfusion (DSC) and permeability (DCE) imaging requires two separate acquisitions, which increases scanning time, and two full CA doses, which raises concerns for chronic gadolinium deposition [ 29 ] and adverse effects in patients with impaired renal function [ 30 ]. Dual-echo DSC simultaneously acquires two GE echoes, which can be processed to disentangle the T 2 *- and T 1 -contributions that coexist in a DSC sequence [ 31 ]. In fact, DSC bears some T 1 -weighting, which can be sorted out by analyzing two GE echoes. The T 1 -contribution can further be used for a DCE analysis, enabling complementary permeability imaging without extra scanning time and without a second CA dose [ 31 ]. Additionally, dual-echo DSC allows to compute quantitative maps derived from CA leakage effects. In the presence of BBB breakdown, CA leaks from the intravascular (IV) to the extravascular extracellular (EEC) compartment, resulting in competing T 2 *- and T 1 -leakage effects, whose balance is influenced by tissue-related factors [ 32 , 33 ]. In a traditional single-echo DSC, the overall balance between T 2 *- and T 1 -leakage effects can be evaluated with a metric named percentage of signal recovery (PSR) [ 34 ], which is valuable for differential diagnosis because tissue-related factors differ among tumor types (gliomas, lymphomas, and meningiomas) [ 34 , 35 ]. However, PSR strongly depends on acquisition parameters such as flip angle (FA) and echo time (TE) [ 36 ], a major obstacle when generalizing reliable PSR cutoffs across institutions. Moreover, PSR only provides overall estimates of the balance between T 2 *- and T 1 -leakage effects, which cannot be disentangled with a single-echo DSC. Conversely, dual-echo DSC allows to separately evaluate T 1 and T 2 * contributions, and to compute a novel quantitative biomarker named transverse relaxivity at tracer equilibrium ( TRATE ), which quantifies T 2 *-leakage effects normalized to the estimated CA concentration (derived from T 1 -leakage effects) [ 32 , 33 ]. Despite bearing similar information to PSR, TRATE is independent from acquisition factors (FA and TE) [ 33 ]. Results from simulated and preclinical data advocate for TRATE as a biomarker for cytoarchitectural features such as cell volume fraction and cell size, but its application on human brain tumors has only been preliminary explored in five recurrent high-grade gliomas [ 33 ]. In this study, we aim to simultaneously obtain perfusion, permeability, and novel leakage effect maps in a cohort of human gliomas, both newly diagnosed and recurrent, using a dynamic spin-and-gradient-echo echoplanar imaging (dynamic SAGE-EPI) acquisition. In fact, the first and second echoes of a dynamic SAGE-EPI can serve as a dual-echo DSC sequence. First, we hypothesize that TRATE will correlate with PSR, and that Δ R 1,ss (quantifying T 1 -leakage effects) will correlate with K trans , since these metrics are considered quantitative markers for cytoarchitecture ( TRATE and PSR) and BBB permeability (Δ R 1,ss and K trans ), respectively. Second, we hypothesize that increased TRATE will reflect aggressive cytoarchitectural features, and will therefore be higher in tumors with higher expression of Ki67 (a marker of cell proliferation) and with IDH wild-type (IDH wt ) status (i.e., glioblastomas).

extracted_data.document_summary: This study investigated the feasibility and biological correlations of simultaneously quantifying perfusion, permeability, and novel contrast leakage effects in brain gliomas using dynamic spin-and-gradient-echo echoplanar imaging (dynamic SAGE-EPI) with a single contrast injection. The research detailed the methodology for acquiring and processing MRI data from 38 adult-type diffuse glioma patients, focusing on parameters like TRATE, ΔR2,ss*, ΔR1,ss, ADC, nrCBV, PSR, Ktrans, and ve. Key findings demonstrate that dynamic SAGE-EPI enables the simultaneous assessment of these parameters, providing new metrics that correlate with previous treatment exposure, IDH status, and Ki67 expression, offering advantages like shorter scan times and reduced contrast agent use, and revealing distinct differences in contrast agent dynamics and tissue properties between treatment-naïve and recurrent gliomas, as well as between IDH-mutant and IDH-wildtype tumors. Specifically, ΔR1,ss shows potential as a quantitative biomarker for blood-brain barrier breakdown, and TRATE captures unique cytoarchitectural information dependent on cell volume fraction and cell size.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Dynamic Spin-and-Gradient-Echo Echoplanar Imaging (dynamic SAGE-EPI) for diagnostic imaging of brain gliomas, sometimes in the context of previous cancer treatment.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A single bolus of Gadavist (Gadobutrol) contrast agent was administered at approximately 0.1 mL/kg (rate ~4 mL/s) for the dynamic SAGE-EPI. This imaging technique reduces scanning time (~3 min) and contrast dose compared to traditional separate acquisitions for perfusion and permeability imaging. The study also analyzed the effects of previous, unspecified cancer treatments (e.g., radiation, chemoradiation) on imaging metrics, but no specific dose or duration details for these prior treatments were reported, nor were any dose-response comparisons for imaging parameters.

analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: MRI metric (Transverse Relaxivity at Tracer Equilibrium), a quantitative biomarker reflecting T2*-leakage effects normalized to estimated contrast agent concentration.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: varies (higher in TN-IDH wt, lower with previous treatment)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Lower TRATE (p = 0.002) observed in IDH wild-type gliomas with previous treatment exposure. TRATE values above 142 mM−1 s−1 were exclusively seen in treatment-naïve IDH wild-type gliomas. It was significantly higher in treatment-naïve IDH wild-type gliomas compared to recurrent IDH wild-type gliomas (p=0.002). TRATE strongly correlated with ΔR2,ss* in TN-gliomas (p=0.004, r=+0.71) and moderately in R-gliomas (p=0.02, r=+0.46). It moderately correlated with ΔR1,ss in R-gliomas (p=0.04, r=−0.42) but not in TN-gliomas (p=0.32). In TN-gliomas, it correlated with ADC (p=0.04, r=−0.54) and nrCBV (p=0.02, r=+0.60). TRATE strongly inversely correlated with PSR in both TN (p<0.0001, r=−0.87) and R (p=0.0003, r=−0.68) gliomas. There was a trend towards higher TRATE in TN-IDH wt than TN-IDH m (p=0.13), and it was higher in TN-gliomas with high Ki67 expression (p=0.04). TRATE > 142 mM−1 s−1 predicted high Ki67 (>10%) with AUC = 0.84, sensitivity = 89%, and specificity = 80%. Its value also varies depending on cell volume fraction and cell size.

analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: MRI metric (Percentage of Signal Recovery), a traditional Dynamic Susceptibility Contrast (DSC) metric reflecting the overall balance between T2*- and T1-leakage effects.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: varies (higher with previous treatment in IDH wt, lower in TN-IDH wt than R-IDH wt, lower with high Ki67)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Higher PSR (p = 0.006) observed in IDH wild-type gliomas with previous treatment exposure. PSR strongly inversely correlated with TRATE in TN (p<0.0001, r=−0.87) and R (p=0.0003, r=−0.68) gliomas. PSR values depended on ΔR2,ss* in both TN- (p=0.02, r=−0.61) and R-gliomas (p=0.03, r=−0.45), but not on ΔR1,ss. It correlated with ADC (p=0.015, r=+0.63) and nrCBV (p=0.005, r=−0.70) in TN-gliomas. Significantly lower in treatment-naïve IDH wild-type gliomas than recurrent IDH wild-type gliomas (p=0.006). It was lower in recurrent IDH wild-type than recurrent gliomas (p=0.006) and lower in TN-gliomas with high Ki67 expression than low Ki67 lesions (p=0.04).

analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: MRI metric (Volume Transfer Constant), a Dynamic Contrast Enhanced (DCE) parameter representing the rate of contrast agent leakage.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: varies (higher with previous treatment, lower in TN vs R)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Higher Ktrans (p = 0.17) observed in IDH wild-type gliomas with previous treatment exposure. Higher Ktrans observed alongside ΔR1,ss (p = 0.026) in IDH-mutant gliomas with previous treatment. Computed voxel-wise by fitting a Tofts model. Strongly correlated with ΔR1,ss in both TN-gliomas (p=0.036, r=+0.68) and R-gliomas (p=0.0024, r=+0.59). Lower in TN-gliomas than R-gliomas (IDH m /IDH wt : p=0.026/0.17). Tended to be higher in TN-IDH wt than TN-IDH m (p=0.09). Average values in glioblastoma cohorts ranged 0.035–1.8 min-1, with 0.16 min-1 in this study. It was also higher with previous exposure to treatment.

analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Brain gliomas (enhancing lesion area), specifically reflecting contrast agent presence in the extravascular extracellular compartment and blood-brain barrier integrity.
analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: MRI metric (ΔR1,ss), derived from changes in longitudinal relaxation rate at steady state, quantifying T1-leakage effects from contrast agent.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: varies (higher with previous treatment, lower in TN vs R)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Higher ΔR1,ss (p = 0.035) observed in IDH wild-type gliomas with previous treatment exposure, and alongside Ktrans (p = 0.026) in IDH-mutant gliomas with previous treatment. Computed voxel-wise by averaging final 10 timepoints of ΔR1(t) curves (assuming T10 of 1.4s). Moderately correlated with TRATE in R-gliomas (p=0.04, r=−0.42) but not TN-gliomas (p=0.32). Not dependent on PSR. Strongly correlated with Ktrans in both TN-gliomas (p=0.036, r=+0.68) and R-gliomas (p=0.0024, r=+0.59). Lower in TN-gliomas compared to R-gliomas (IDH m /IDH wt : p=0.026/0.035). Tended to be higher in TN-IDH wt than TN-IDH m (p=0.13). Higher values are indicative of greater blood-brain barrier breakdown.

analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: MRI metric (ΔR2,ss*), representing the change in transverse relaxation rate at steady state, reflecting T2*-leakage effects.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Obtained voxel-wise; computed by averaging the final 10 timepoints of the ΔR2*(t) time curves. Strongly correlated with TRATE in TN-gliomas (p=0.004, r=+0.71) and moderately in R-gliomas (p=0.02, r=+0.46). PSR values depended on ΔR2,ss* in both TN- (p=0.02, r=−0.61) and R-gliomas (p=0.03, r=−0.45). It was comparable between TN-IDH wt and R-IDH wt despite less concentrated EEC CA in TN-IDH wt. Tended to be higher in TN-IDH wt than TN-IDH m (p=0.09). Differences greatly exceeded ΔR1,ss differences.

analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: MRI metric (Normalized Relative Cerebral Blood Volume), a Dynamic Susceptibility Contrast (DSC) perfusion metric.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Generated with bidirectional leakage correction and normalized to the cerebral median rCBV. Correlated with TRATE in TN-gliomas (p=0.02, r=+0.60) but not in R-gliomas. Correlated with PSR in TN-gliomas (p=0.005, r=−0.70). Tended to differ depending on IDH status in TN-gliomas (p=0.09). It was the only metric with significantly different values based on IDH status in the recurrent setting. Higher in TN-gliomas with high Ki67 expression (p=0.001).

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Binarized as 'less than or equal to 10%' or 'greater than 10%'. High Ki67 expression (>10%) was predicted by TRATE > 142 mM−1 s−1 with AUC = 0.84 (sensitivity = 89%, specificity = 80%). High Ki67 expression was associated with higher TRATE (p=0.04), higher nrCBV (p=0.001), and lower PSR (p=0.04).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Cell proliferation marker; biomarker of active cell proliferation.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Histopathological diagnosis of adult-type diffuse glioma; Treatment-naïve (TN) gliomas.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates tumor proliferative activity, which is associated with tumor aggressiveness and grade; indicates active cell proliferation; associated with higher cellularity and proliferation rate in IDH wt gliomas.

analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Inferred rate from MRI metrics (Ktrans, ΔR1,ss).

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Slower CA leakage rate is reflected by lower Ktrans in treatment-naïve gliomas compared to recurrent gliomas. Treatment-naïve IDH wild-type gliomas tended to have more pronounced CA leakage (higher ΔR1,ss and Ktrans) than treatment-naïve IDH-mutant gliomas.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: The speed at which contrast agent passes from the blood vessels into the surrounding tissue, indicative of vascular permeability.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Glioma characterization based on treatment status (treatment-naïve vs recurrent) and IDH status.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Reflects vascular permeability and microenvironmental characteristics in gliomas, which can be important for assessing tumor aggressiveness and response to treatment.
